# lnurlcash-kit (Python)

LNURLcash (LUD-25) bearer note client for Python 3.10+. MIT.

pip install lnurlcash-kit

## What this is

LNURLcash notes are LUD-03 withdrawRequest links whose k1 IS the asset:
lnurlw://mint.example/w?k1=<32-byte-hex>&amount=<msat>. Whoever knows the k1
can spend it. Amounts are ALWAYS integer milli-satoshis.

Draft spec: https://github.com/lnurl/luds/pull/301
Reference mint: https://github.com/dni/lnurl-mint

## Core API

from lnurlcash_kit import LnurlcashClient, AsyncLnurlcashClient

client = LnurlcashClient(timeout=30.0, offline=False, rng=generate_note_secret,
                         policy=Policy(), mutation_retries=1)
Policy(require_signatures=False, require_mint_pubkey=True) is the default.

client.fetch_note_info(url) -> WithdrawRequestInfo(callback, k1, max_withdrawable, mint_pubkey)
client.rotate_note(callback, k1) -> RotateResult(k1, signature)
client.split_note(callback, k1s, amount_msat) -> SplitResult(k1, change, signature, change_signature)
client.merge_notes(callback, k1s) -> RotateResult
client.melt_note(callback, k1, bolt11) -> MeltResult(pr, verify)
client.settle_note(base_url, k1, expected_msat, sig) -> (k1, amount_msat, sig, callback)
client.probe_burned_note(url) -> 'live' | 'gone' | 'unknown'
client.fetch_pay_request(url) / request_invoice(cb, msat) / fetch_invoice_verification(url)
client.fetch_mint_address(url)

verify_note_signature(k1, amount_msat, sig_hex, mint_pubkey_hex) -> bool
  k1 may be a ck1 and sig a cs1 (LUD-25 Part 2, below)
resolve_note_input(text) / resolve_mint_input(text) / resolve_lnurl_input(text)
parse_mint_fee(metadata) / apply_mint_fee(gross, fee) / gross_up_for_mint_fee(net, fee)

AsyncLnurlcashClient has the identical surface with await.

For a different HTTP stack use lnurlcash_kit.protocol directly: each function
returns Request(url, parse, new_secrets) and performs no I/O.

## Rules an implementation MUST follow

1. max_withdrawable from fetch_note_info is the ONLY authoritative value. The
   `amount` in a note URL is an unverified claim.
2. On rotate/split/merge the WALLET generates the replacement secret and
   discloses only sha256(secret). Never accept a service-supplied k1.
3. Catch AmbiguousMutation, PERSIST err.new_secrets before anything else, then
   call probe_burned_note. Treating it as failure destroys money the service
   may already have minted.
4. RequestRefused means nothing was sent - safe to treat as a no-op.
5. A melt's OK means IN FLIGHT, not spent. NotePending means retry, not spent.
5b. A cp1 note is owed its certificate; a plain note is UNSIGNED. LUD-25 Part
   2 certifies cp1 outputs only: a rotate/split/merge to a cp1 output (p1, or
   p2 for a split's change) MUST return its cs1 in sig (sig2 for the change),
   and a missing one raises UnverifiableNote WHATEVER the policy says. A hash
   output comes back with signature None by design; that is not an error.
   UnverifiableNote means the mutation LANDED, so keep its secrets (empty
   after a *_with_hash call: the caller already holds that key).
   Policy(require_signatures=True) also demands the old Part 1 signature over
   a hash. Policy(require_mint_pubkey=True), the default, refuses a
   withdrawRequest with no valid mintPubkey; set False for a Part 1-only mint.
5c. A retried rotate/split/merge MUST be answered by the service as a replay of
   the original success, so a client re-sends one whose answer was lost
   (mutation_retries, default 1) and usually completes it. NEVER a melt. The
   IDENTICAL request goes out: the replay is matched on the k1 set, h, h2 and
   amount, so a fresh secret would make it a different mutation.
6. Rotate immediately after claiming a minted note: the mint generated that
   preimage, and LUD-21 verify exposes it to anyone who saw the invoice.
7. Never log note URLs. The secret is in the query string.
8. Never branch on exception message text. Branch on the class.

## Errors

RequestRefused     nothing sent, note untouched
ServiceRejected    processed and refused (definitive)
  NotePending      a melt is in flight on this k1 - retry
UnverifiableNote   the mutation LANDED without a signature it owed: a cp1
                   output's cs1, or a hash output's Part 1 signature under
                   require_signatures=True. The note is REAL; carries
                   .new_secrets - persist them
new_secrets_of(err) the secrets carried by ANY exception that could describe a
                   mutation the service applied: ambiguous, unverifiable, spent
                   or unknown
  NoteSpent        authoritative: already burned
  NoteUnknown      service does not recognise it
AmbiguousMint      outcome UNKNOWN - assume nothing
  AmbiguousMutation  carries .new_secrets - persist them
ProtocolError      a non-mutating response did not match the spec

## Conformance

https://github.com/TheCryptoDonkey/lnurlcash-conformance

Seed-recoverable note secrets (LUD-25):
derive_cash_root(seed) -> CashNode              BIP-32 m/139'
derive_cash_domain_node(root, host) -> CashNode m/139'/d1/d2/d3/d4, d1..d4 =
  HMAC-SHA256(privkey at m/139'/0, host)[0..16] as 4 RAW big-endian uint32.
  RAW: BIP-32 reads >= 2^31 as hardened, so ~half the levels are, decided by
  the host name. NEVER mask the top bit, NEVER harden all four - either
  derives a different tree and restores nothing, silently.
derive_cash_secret(root, host, i) / cash_secret_at(domain_node, i)
  no unhardened level below the domain node, so a signer given the node needs
  no curve - which is why the node is its own step
cash_node_to_hex / cash_node_from_hex   privateKey || chainCode, 64 bytes
derive_cash_child(node, raw_uint32)     BIP-32 CKDpriv, for checking this
  library against BIP-32's own vectors
CashSecretSource(root, host, start)()   -> k1; .next_index is what you persist
derive_note_root / derive_note_secret   LEGACY pre-spec HMAC scheme. Do not
  mint under it; still scanned so old notes stay findable.
build_note_info_url_by_hash(link, h) / note_info_by_hash_request(link, h)
  the ?h= informational GET, so a restore walk keeps secrets off the wire.
  A rejection proves nothing: unsupported, unknown and BURNED are one answer.
  The persisted per-host counter is the real backup, not the scan.

LUD-25 Part 2, notes keyed by a public key (lnurlcash_kit.recoverable):
The holder keeps sk and discloses pk as cp1. The k1 that SPENDS the note is a
ck1: a recoverable signature by sk over "LNURLcash". cs1 is the mint's
certificate, cx1 a watch-only branch (x-only pubkey || chain code). All four
are bech32m, fixed length, no 90-char limit, upper case fine, mixed case
refused. Decoders return None, never raise.
encode_cp1/ck1/cs1(bytes) -> str   decode_cp1/ck1/cs1(str) -> bytes | None
encode_cx1(pubkey_x_only, chain_code) / decode_cx1(str) -> Cx1 | None
is_cp1 / is_ck1 / is_cs1 / is_cx1(str) -> bool
derive_cash_address_node(root, host) -> CashNode   m/139'/1'/d1/d2/d3/d4,
  d1..d4 = HMAC-SHA256(privkey at m/139'/1'/0, host), raw as in Part 1. The
  REFERENCE WALLET'S path. The spec text's m/139'/d1..d4 is the Part 1
  ladder's node and restores nothing.
cash_node_to_cx1(node) -> Cx1   hand this out, never the node
derive_note_pubkey(branch_pubkey_x_only, chain_code, i) -> 32-byte x-only
  watch-only. t = tagged_hash("LNURLcash/derive", P || chain_code ||
  ser32_be(i)); i is any uint32, never hardened. t >= n or a zero key raises
  ProtocolError: use the next i. Never reduced.
derive_note_secret_key(branch_private_key, chain_code, i) -> 32 bytes
sign_note_ownership(sk) -> 65 bytes r || s || recid, RFC6979, low-S
recover_note_ownership_pubkey(sig) -> x-only pk | None
note_id_of(k1) -> sha256 hex for a hex k1, recovered pk hex for a ck1, else None
  One note has MANY valid ck1 strings. Compare notes by this, never by k1.
  fetch_note_info's echo check does: another ck1 for the same note passes,
  a different note is refused.
note_lookup_of(k1) -> the hash, or the cp1 for a ck1. Pass it to
  note_info_by_hash_request: a cp1 goes as ?p=, a hash as ?h=. The answer's
  .signature is the note's cs1.
Wire: a ck1 goes anywhere a k1 does (note URL, fetch_note_info, rotate, split,
  merge, melt). A cp1 output goes as p1/p2 from the *_with_hash calls, while a
  hash keeps h/h2. mint_invoice_request_with_hash sends a cp1 as the comment
  alone.
verify_note_signature_hash(pk_hex, amount_msat, cs1, mint_pubkey) -> bool
  for a cx1 watcher, which has the key but never a ck1
derive_cash_master(seed) -> CashNode   BIP-32 master, for paths not named here
EXTENSION, not LUD-25: derive_nostr_cash_seed(sk) = HMAC-SHA256(key = sk,
  msg = "LNURLcash/nostr-seed"); derive_nostr_address_node(sk, host) = the
  address path above from that seed. sk is the raw 32 bytes an nsec encodes.
